papers.title: Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series Using Locally Coupled Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: The analysis of nonstationary time series is of great importance in many scientific fields such as physics and neuroscience. In recent years, Gaussian process regression has attracted substantial attention as a robust and powerful method for analyzing time series. In this paper, we introduce a new framework for analyzing nonstationary time series using locally stationary Gaussian process analysis with parameters that are coupled through a hidden Markov model. The main advantage of this framework is that arbitrary complex nonstationary covariance functions can be obtained by combining simpler stationary building blocks whose hidden parameters can be estimated in closed-form. We demonstrate the flexibility of the method by analyzing two examples of synthetic nonstationary signals: oscillations with time varying frequency and time series with two dynamical states. Finally, we report an example application on real magnetoencephalographic measurements of brain activity.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, lacks implant mechanics or biomedical engineering context, and does not involve optimization or constraints handling.

summary_en.motivation: To analyze nonstationary time series in fields such as physics and neuroscience using a flexible Gaussian process framework.
summary_en.method: A locally coupled Gaussian process model is introduced where parameters are coupled through a hidden Markov model, enabling closed-form estimation of nonstationary covariance functions.
summary_en.result: The method effectively captures time-varying frequency oscillations and transitions between two dynamical states in synthetic data and real magnetoencephalographic recordings.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on synthetic nonstationary signals and real magnetoencephalographic brain activity measurements.

papers.title: Severe metallosis following oxidised zirconium wear in total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: We present a case of a man aged 81 years who underwent a primary cementless total hip arthroplasty. Eight years after the index surgery, failure of the arthroplasty was revealed by the presence of the radiographic ‘cloud sign’ (figure 1). The original components used were the R3 acetabular cup with a Synergy femoral stem, highly crossed linked polyethylene liner and an oxidised zirconium (Oxinium) femoral head (Smith & Nephew Synergy, Memphis, Tennessee, USA). llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为全髋关节置换术后金属病的病例报告，未涉及应力遮挡或微动的力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical case report on metallosis due to wear, containing no finite element analysis, stress shielding quantification, micromotion simulation, or boundary condition data for femoral stem biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 报告一例全髋置换术后氧化锆股骨头磨损导致的严重金属病。
summary_zh.method: 通过影像学（云征）和血液检测诊断金属病。
summary_zh.result: 患者因磨损颗粒引发假体周围金属沉积和骨质溶解。
summary_zh.validation: 临床病例观察与影像学证实。

summary_en.motivation: This case report documents severe metallosis caused by wear of an oxidized zirconium femoral head after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Diagnosis based on radiographic 'cloud sign' (CT) and blood tests for metal ion levels.
summary_en.result: The wear debris led to periprosthetic metallosis and osteolysis, requiring revision surgery.
summary_en.validation: Confirmed through clinical presentation, imaging, and intraoperative findings.
